details:
**Beloved and Sethe**
Morrison's most famous novel (1987), and the giveaway in nearly every question. Sethe, who escaped slavery, killed her infant daughter (cutting her throat with a handsaw in a woodshed) rather than let slave catchers take her back, and the girl returns years later as a ghost and then as a mysterious young woman named Beloved; the story is loosely based on the escaped slave Margaret Garner.

**124 Bluestone Road**
The house outside Cincinnati where Sethe lives with her daughter Denver, haunted by the baby's ghost. The novel opens "124 was spiteful. Full of a baby's venom," and Sethe's mother-in-law Baby Suggs, a preacher, dies there.

**Paul D and the tobacco tin**
A former slave from Sweet Home who arrives at 124 years later, drives out the ghost, and becomes Sethe's lover. He survived a chain gang in Georgia and escaped by following blossoming trees north, and he keeps his painful memories locked away in a rusted "tobacco tin" where his heart should be; he tells Sethe her love is "too thick."

**Sweet Home and Schoolteacher**
The Kentucky plantation where Sethe, Paul D, Halle (Sethe's husband), and Sixo were enslaved. After the kind Mr. Garner dies, the cruel Schoolteacher takes over, measures the slaves' features, and later has Sixo burned alive; Mrs. Garner had given Sethe a pair of crystal earrings as a wedding gift.

**Denver, Amy Denver, and Mr. Bodwin**
Sethe's surviving daughter, Denver, is named after Amy Denver, the white girl who helped deliver her during Sethe's escape. At the climax, the women of the town gather to exorcise Beloved, and Sethe attacks the white abolitionist Mr. Bodwin with an icepick, mistaking him for Schoolteacher coming to take her children; Stamp Paid, who ferried Sethe across the Ohio River, saved Denver from Sethe's attack.

**Song of Solomon and Milkman Dead**
Morrison's 1977 novel about Macon "Milkman" Dead III, nicknamed by the janitor Freddie because his mother breastfed him until he was too old. He travels south to Shalimar, Virginia, to search for hidden family gold and instead learns that his great-grandfather Solomon flew back to Africa; the novel opens with the insurance agent Robert Smith jumping off the roof of Mercy Hospital, and Milkman is born the next day.

**Guitar Bains and the Seven Days**
Milkman's best friend in Song of Solomon, who joins the Seven Days, a secret society that kills a white person in the same way, and on the same day of the week, as each Black victim of racist violence. Guitar comes to believe Milkman stole the gold, accidentally shoots Pilate, and the novel ends with Milkman leaping toward him.

**Pilate Dead**
Milkman's aunt in Song of Solomon, born without a navel. Her father chose her name blindly from the Bible, as the family names its children (Milkman's sisters are First Corinthians and Magdalene); a green sack hanging in her house that Milkman and Guitar steal, thinking it holds gold, actually contains her father's bones, and her granddaughter Hagar repeatedly tries to kill Milkman.

**The Bluest Eye and Pecola Breedlove**
Morrison's first novel (1970), about Pecola Breedlove, a young Black girl who idolizes Shirley Temple and longs for blue eyes, believing they would make her beautiful. She is raped by her father Cholly, and after her baby dies she goes mad, believing she has the bluest eyes.

**Claudia MacTeer, Dick and Jane, and the marigolds**
The Bluest Eye is narrated mainly by Claudia MacTeer, whose family takes Pecola in for a while, and its section titles come from a run-together "Dick and Jane" primer. Claudia and her sister plant marigold seeds that fail to bloom in 1941, mirroring the death of Pecola's baby.

**Soaphead Church**
A pedophile "spiritualist" in The Bluest Eye whom Pecola asks for blue eyes. He tricks her into feeding poisoned meat to his landlady's old dog, Bob, telling her that if the dog reacts, her wish will be granted.

**Sula, Nel Wright, and Chicken Little**
Sula (1973) follows the friendship of Sula Peace and Nel Wright in the Bottom, a Black neighborhood of Medallion, Ohio. As girls, Sula accidentally swings the boy Chicken Little into a river, where he drowns, and she later returns to town after ten years "accompanied by a plague of robins" and has an affair with Ajax; her one-legged grandmother Eva burns her son Plum to death.

**Shadrack and National Suicide Day**
A shell-shocked World War I veteran in Sula who founds National Suicide Day, held every January 3. Sula visits his shack right after Chicken Little drowns.

**"Recitatif"**
Morrison's only published short story, which opens "My mother danced all night." It follows Twyla and Roberta, who meet at the St. Bonny's orphanage and later end up picketing on opposite sides over school busing, while never revealing which of the two is Black and which is white.

**Later novels (Jazz, A Mercy, Tar Baby, Paradise, Love, Home)**
In Jazz, Joe Trace shoots his young lover Dorcas, and his wife Violet slashes the dead girl's face at her funeral; A Mercy follows Florens, Lina, and Sorrow, who serve the Dutch trader Jacob Vaark and his wife Rebekka in the 1600s; Tar Baby features the romance of the Sorbonne-educated Jadine and Son; Paradise opens with men from the town of Ruby attacking a convent full of women; Love centers on Heed and Christine fighting over Bill Cosey's estate; and Home follows the Korean War veteran Frank Money rescuing his sister Cee. Morrison won the 1993 Nobel Prize in Literature.
